sources.entry: PairDrop | Local file sharing in your browser, inspired by AirDrop

summary.one_liner: PairDrop is a self-hostable, browser-based file and text sharing app for local networks and the Internet, inspired by Apple's AirDrop and forked from Snapdrop.
summary.what_it_does: PairDrop lets devices send images, documents, or text to each other peer-to-peer through a web browser, with devices on the same local network discovering each other automatically. It supports persistent device pairing via a 6-digit code or QR code, so paired devices can find each other even across different networks. Temporary public rooms, entered with a 5-letter code or QR code, allow file transfers over the Internet. Files are sent after the recipient accepts the request, multiple files are downloaded as a ZIP, and transfers show overall progress. The README also mentions sending from the Share menu on iOS and Android, from the context menu on Ubuntu (Nautilus) and Windows, and via a command-line interface. It can be hosted yourself with Docker or Node.js.
use_cases: share files between phone and laptop
send photos in original quality to Android and iOS users
transfer files peer-to-peer on a local network
share files over the Internet with temporary rooms
self-host a local AirDrop alternative on a Raspberry Pi
send files from the command line or file manager context menu
how_to_run: Host your own instance with Docker or Node.js (see project documentation for exact commands)
notable: Persistent device pairing via 6-digit code or QR code that works across networks
Temporary public rooms for Internet transfers without accounts
Automatic TURN relay for devices behind NAT
Send directly from Share menus, OS context menus, or CLI
caveats: Internet transfers between devices behind NAT depend on the TURN server (the README notes the PairDrop TURN server for auto-connection)
Public rooms are temporary; closing PairDrop leaves all rooms
Share-menu and context-menu integrations are listed for specific platforms only (iOS, Android, Ubuntu/Nautilus, Windows)
